mainTopic: The two פורים verses, how מגילת אסתר became Scripture and its holiness, proofs that it was said with רוח הקודש, and the minimum amounts for משלוח מנות and מתנות לאביונים.
overview: This amud finishes the leap-year discussion. It explains why both "השנית" and "בכל שנה ושנה" are needed to keep פורים once, in אדר שני, and what רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי learns from "השנית" instead. Next come two versions of אסתר's request to the חכמים: to make פורים permanent, and to write her book into תנ"ך. In the second version the חכמים find room for the מגילה in the פסוק "כתב זאת זכרון בספר", a reading that matches a dispute between רבי יהושע and רבי אלעזר המודעי. שמואל rules that ספר אסתר does not make the hands טמא, because it was given to be read, not written, and he follows רבי יהושע. Side discussions cover קהלת and שיר השירים. Several תנאים then bring proofs that אסתר was said with רוח הקודש. רבא knocks down every proof except שמואל's "קיימו וקבלו", and רב יוסף and רב נחמן בר יצחק add proofs of their own. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה: משלוח מנות is two portions to one person, and מתנות לאביונים is two gifts to two poor people. It then begins a story of a פורים gift that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why both verses are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל needs both "השנית" and "בכל שנה ושנה". Each verse blocks a different mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: [We learn from the word] "the second", and we also needed the Torah to write "in each and every year". With only "in each and every year", I would have read it like our earlier question, meaning the אדר right after שבט. So "the second" teaches us it is the second אדר. With only "the second", I would have said we should ideally keep פורים in both the first and the second אדר. So "in each and every year" teaches us that, just like every year, we keep פורים only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that each of the two verses is needed. Each one alone could be misread, so we need both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "בכל שנה ושנה" alone could suggest the אדר next to שבט, which is אדר ראשון. "השנית" fixes that and points to אדר שני. "השנית" alone could suggest keeping פורים twice, and "בכל שנה ושנה" fixes that: just like a normal year, there is only one פורים.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: "השנית" puts פורים in אדר שני, and "בכל שנה ושנה" makes sure it is kept only once.

phrases.english: "The second"
and it was necessary to write "in each and every year".
For if [we learned only] from "in each and every year",
I would have said it means what our question suggested,
phrases.notes: "Our question" is the earlier idea that "every year" means the אדר that comes right after שבט.

phrases.english: so it teaches us "the second".
And if it had taught us only "the second",
I would have said that from the outset [we keep it] in the first and in the second [אדר],
phrases.notes: Here "בתחילה" means "ideally, right from the start". It does not mean "at first" as it does in the next step.

phrases.english: so it teaches us "in each and every year".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier derivation of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל by explaining why he needs two verses.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each source is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With one verse alone, we might think פורים is in אדר ראשון, or in both אדרים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both verses together teach one פורים, in אדר שני.

steps.title: What does the other opinion do with "the second"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי uses the word "השנית", since he does not use it to place פורים in אדר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי, what does he do with this word "the second"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other opinion and asks how he explains a word his opponent relies on. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי holds that פורים is in אדר ראשון, so "השנית" cannot mean אדר שני for him. Every word of a פסוק must teach something, so the גמרא wants to know what this one teaches him.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it (how does he use this verse)?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Yosei,
this word "the second", what does he do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's use of "השנית" to the other opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי learns from "השנית"

steps.title: "The second" teaches that פורים spread from שושן to the world
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי uses "השנית" for רב שמואל בר יהודה's teaching: פורים was first set in שושן and later for the whole world.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for the teaching of רב שמואל בר יהודה. רב שמואל בר יהודה said: at first they set up פורים in שושן, and later in the whole world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word "השנית" has a different job for רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי. It refers to a second stage, when פורים spread worldwide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For him, "השנית" means the second letter about פורים, not the second אדר. The first letter set פורים only in שושן, and the second spread it to every Jewish community.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)

phrases.aramaic: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: He needs it for that [teaching] of Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda,
as Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda said:
At first they established it in Shushan,
and in the end in the entire world.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "השנית" teaches that פורים was first set in שושן and later for the whole world.
steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions use "השנית". רבן שמעון בן גמליאל reads it as אדר שני, and רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי reads it as the second stage of setting up פורים.

steps.title: אסתר asks the חכמים to set up פורים for all generations
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה relates that אסתר asked the חכמים to make פורים permanent. They feared it would stir up the nations, and she answered that the story was already publicly recorded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יהודה said: אסתר sent to the חכמים, "Establish me for all generations!" They sent back, "You will stir up anger against us among the nations." She sent back, "I am already written in the official records of the kings of Media and Persia."
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב שמואל בר יהודה was just quoted about how פורים was set up, the גמרא brings another teaching of his on the same topic. It tells how אסתר pushed for פורים to become permanent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים worried that a yearly celebration of the Jews' victory over their enemies would anger the nations. אסתר replied that the story was already in the Persian royal records. Reading it every year would reveal nothing the world did not already know.

keyTerms.meaning: Establish me (my holiday) for all generations

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda said:
Esther sent to the Sages:
Establish me for [all] generations!
They sent to her:

phrases.aramaic: קִנְאָה אַתְּ מְעוֹרֶרֶת עָלֵינוּ לְבֵין הָאוּמּוֹת.
phrases.english: You are stirring up anger against us among the nations.
She sent to them:
I am already written

phrases.aramaic: עַל דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים לְמַלְכֵי מָדַי וּפָרָס.
phrases.english: in the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another teaching of רב שמואל בר יהודה about how פורים was set up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אסתר convinced the חכמים to make פורים permanent, because the story was already publicly known.

steps.title: A second version: אסתר asks that her book be written in תנ"ך
steps.stepSummary: Four אמוראים teach that אסתר asked the חכמים to write her book into Scripture. The חכמים answered from a פסוק that the עמלק story is to be written three times, not four.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב, רב חנינא, רבי יוחנן and רב חביבא taught the following. (Throughout סדר מועד, wherever this pair appears, take out רבי יוחנן and put in רבי יונתן.) אסתר sent to the חכמים, "Write me for all generations." They sent back, "It says: 'Have I not written for you three times', meaning three times and not four."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of אסתר's request, this time about writing the מגילה into תנ"ך. Along the way it notes a correction to one name. This is the opening of a story that continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the issue is whether the מגילה can become part of Scripture, not just whether פורים is kept. The war with עמלק already appears three times in תנ"ך, and the חכמים read the פסוק "שלישים" (three times) as a limit. A book about המן, a descendant of עמלק, would make a forbidden fourth time.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of the Talmud dealing with holidays

steps.confusionAlert: "קבעוני" in the step before and "כתבוני" here are two different requests. The first asks to make the holiday permanent, and the second asks to make the book part of תנ"ך.

phrases.aramaic: רַב וְרַב חֲנִינָא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַב חֲבִיבָא מַתְנוּ.
phrases.english: Rav, and Rav Ḥanina, and Rabbi Yoḥanan, and Rav Ḥaviva taught:
Throughout the whole order of Moed,
wherever this pair [of names] appears,
phrases.notes: "This pair" is the last two names, רבי יוחנן and רב חביבא.

phrases.aramaic: חַלּוֹפֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וּמְעַיֵּיל רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן.
phrases.english: take out Rabbi Yoḥanan and put in Rabbi Yonatan.
Esther sent to the Sages:
Write me for [all] generations.
They sent to her:
"Have I not written for you three times",
phrases.notes: This is a פסוק in משלי (22:20).

phrases.english: three times and not four times,
phrases.notes: The fight with עמלק is already written three times in תנ"ך, so adding אסתר's story would make a fourth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וְרַב חֲנִינָא וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַב חֲבִיבָא מַתְנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel version of אסתר's request, now about including the book in Scripture.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים first pushed back on writing the מגילה into Scripture, based on "שלישים ולא רבעים". The story continues next.
steps.whyThisMatters: This opens the discussion of how מגילת אסתר became part of תנ"ך, which the next passage continues.

steps.title: The חכמים find a פסוק that makes room for the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים read "כתב זאת זכרון בספר" as three parts: the תורה (שמות and דברים together), the נביאים, and the מגילה. So the מגילה is the third writing, not the fourth.
steps.simpleTranslation: They kept refusing until they found a verse written in the תורה: "Write this as a memorial in the book." "Write this" means what is written here in שמות and also in דברים. "A memorial" means what is written in the נביאים. "In the book" means what is written in the מגילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The story from Step 5 continues. The חכמים had refused אסתר's request, and now they find a way to read the פסוק that allows her book to be written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5 the problem was "three times, not four." Here the two mentions of עמלק in the תורה (שמות and דברים) count as one, under "כתב זאת." That frees up "בספר" to point to the מגילה, so the count stays at three.

keyTerms.meaning: "Write this as a memorial in the book", the פסוק about wiping out עמלק

steps.confusionAlert: Do not count four places here. The תורה's two mentions of עמלק (שמות and דברים) are grouped together as ONE, so the מגילה comes out as the third.

phrases.english: until they found for it a verse
written in the Torah:
"Write this as a memorial in the book."
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק in שמות right after the war with עמלק.

phrases.english: "Write this": what is written here
phrases.notes: "Here" means in שמות, where this פסוק appears.

phrases.english: and in Deuteronomy.
"A memorial": what is written in the Prophets,
"In the book": what is written in the Megillah.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁמָּצְאוּ לוֹ מִקְרָא כָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection the חכמים raised in Step 5 ("three, not four").
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק so the count of three still works
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Writing אסתר would make a fourth account of עמלק, which the פסוק does not allow.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה's two accounts count as one, so the מגילה is the third and may be written.

steps.title: The same reading matches a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records two readings of the פסוק. רבי יהושע counts שמות, דברים and נביאים, which leaves no room for the מגילה. רבי אלעזר המודעי reads it the way the חכמים did in Step 6.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים. "Write this" means what is written here in שמות; "a memorial" means what is written in דברים; "in the book" means what is written in the נביאים. These are the words of רבי יהושע. רבי אלעזר המודעי says: "Write this" means what is written here and in דברים; "a memorial" means what is written in the נביאים; "in the book" means what is written in the מגילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the two ways of reading this פסוק were already argued about by תנאים in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע gives each part of the פסוק its own place: שמות, דברים, and נביאים. That uses up all three parts, so the מגילה has no hint here. רבי אלעזר המודעי joins שמות and דברים together, which leaves "בספר" for the מגילה, just like the reading in Step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: "Like the תנאים": this question matches an earlier dispute between תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהושע, the פסוק covers only the תורה and נביאים. According to רבי אלעזר המודעי, it also includes the מגילה, so the מגילה belongs among the written books.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute of the tanna'im:
"Write this": what is written here,
phrases.notes: Here "here" means שמות alone, without דברים.

phrases.english: "A memorial": what is written in Deuteronomy,
"In the book": what is written in the Prophets.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehoshua.
Rabbi Elazar HaModa'i says:

phrases.aramaic: ״כְּתֹב זֹאת״ — מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב כָּאן וּבְמִשְׁנֵה תוֹרָה,
phrases.english: "Write this": what is written here and in Deuteronomy,
"A memorial": what is written in the Prophets,
"In the book": what is written in the Megillah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the reading in Step 6 matches one side of an existing dispute between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע's reading of the פסוק leaves no room for the מגילה, while רבי אלעזר המודעי's reading includes it.

steps.title: שמואל says אסתר does not make the hands טמא
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports in the name of שמואל that ספר אסתר does not make the hands טמא, unlike other holy books.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that שמואל said: ספר אסתר does not make the hands טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement is brought: שמואל holds that ספר אסתר does not carry the טומאת ידים that the חכמים placed on holy books.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים decreed that touching a holy book makes a person's hands טמא, as a sign of the book's holiness. If אסתר does not do this, it seems שמואל does not treat it as a full holy book. That is what sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes the hands טמא, a rule the חכמים set for holy books

steps.confusionAlert: Not making the hands טמא is a sign of LESS holiness here, not more. The rule of טומאת ידים applies only to books treated as holy Scripture.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Esther does not render the hands impure.
phrases.notes: The חכמים decreed that holy books make hands טמא. Here שמואל says ספר אסתר does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how אסתר was written into Scripture to a הלכה about how holy the book is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ספר אסתר does not make the hands טמא.

steps.title: But שמואל himself said אסתר was said with רוח הקודש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל thinks אסתר was not said with רוח הקודש. That cannot be, since שמואל himself said it was.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean שמואל holds that אסתר was not said with רוח הקודש? But שמואל said that אסתר was said with רוח הקודש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sees a contradiction between two statements of שמואל and challenges the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אסתר does not make the hands טמא, it sounds like it is not a holy book, meaning it was not said with רוח הקודש. But elsewhere שמואל clearly says it was said with רוח הקודש. So his two statements seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is this to say...?", introducing a challenging conclusion
"But didn't he say...?", bringing a contradicting statement

phrases.english: Is this to say that Shmuel holds
that Esther was not said with the Divine Spirit?
But didn't Shmuel say:
Esther was said with the Divine Spirit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's statement in Step 8 using another statement of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that אסתר does not make the hands טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not making the hands טמא suggests the book lacks רוח הקודש, but שמואל himself says it has רוח הקודש.

steps.title: Said with רוח הקודש to be read, not to be written
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רוח הקודש gave אסתר to be read aloud, but not to be written as a holy book. That is why it does not make the hands טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said with רוח הקודש to be read, but it was not said to be written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting what רוח הקודש gave: reading, but not writing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of שמואל's statements are true. אסתר was said with רוח הקודש so that it would be read in public. But it was not given as a book to be written with the holiness of Scripture, so the rule of טומאת ידים does not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: To be written as a holy book

steps.whatToRemember: For שמואל, ספר אסתר came through רוח הקודש for reading, not for writing as Scripture. That is why it does not make the hands טמא.

phrases.english: It was said to be read,
and it was not said to be written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the scope of רוח הקודש: reading versus writing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying אסתר was said with רוח הקודש means it is a fully holy written book.
steps.terutzMaskana: רוח הקודש covered only its public reading, not its writing as Scripture, so it does not make the hands טמא.

steps.title: A ברייתא where everyone agrees אסתר makes the hands טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר, רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון argue about קהלת and שיר השירים. רבי שמעון says everyone agrees that אסתר makes the hands טמא, which goes against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this. רבי מאיר says: קהלת does not make the hands טמא, and there is an argument about שיר השירים. רבי יוסי says: שיר השירים makes the hands טמא, and there is an argument about קהלת. רבי שמעון says: קהלת is one of the cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict. But רות, שיר השירים and אסתר all make the hands טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's statement from Step 8 that אסתר does not make the hands טמא. It brings a ברייתא where אסתר is treated as a holy book that does make the hands טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three תנאים argue about קהלת and שיר השירים, but none of them argues about אסתר. רבי שמעון says plainly that רות, שיר השירים and אסתר make the hands טמא. That is the opposite of what שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes the hands טמא; a rule חז״ל made for holy books

keyTerms.term: מִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
keyTerms.meaning: A case where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'makes the hands טמא' is a sign of holiness. A book that makes the hands טמא is being treated as a holy book, so this is a good thing for the book.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabbi Meir says:
Koheles does not make the hands impure,
and there is a dispute about Shir HaShirim.
Rabbi Yosei says:
Shir HaShirim makes the hands impure,
and there is a dispute about Koheles.
Rabbi Shimon says:
Koheles is one of the leniencies of Beis Shammai
and one of the stringencies of Beis Hillel,
but Ruth, Shir HaShirim and Esther
all make the hands impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling from Step 8 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that ספר אסתר does not make the hands טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, רבי שמעון says everyone agrees that אסתר makes the hands טמא, the opposite of what שמואל said.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל holds like רבי יהושע, who did not count the מגילה in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said his view following רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by saying he follows a different תנא, רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7, רבי יהושע read 'כתב זאת זכרון בספר' as שמות, דברים and נביאים, which leaves no room for the מגילה. So שמואל has a תנא who backs him, even if the ברייתא in Step 11 disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: He said it following the view of...

phrases.english: He said it in line with Rabbi Yehoshua.
phrases.notes: He means שמואל, and the רבי יהושע quoted back in Step 7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the Amora inside a dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל goes against an agreed ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי יהושע, who did not count the מגילה as a written holy book.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's view that אסתר does not make the hands טמא matches רבי יהושע's reading of 'כתב זאת זכרון בספר'.

steps.title: קהלת is only the wisdom of שלמה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says קהלת does not make the hands טמא, because it is שלמה's own wisdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says that קהלת does not make the hands טמא, because it is the wisdom of שלמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. In it רבי שמעון בן מנסיא gives a reason why קהלת is not treated as a holy book.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is that קהלת comes from שלמה's own wisdom, not from רוח הקודש. Without רוח הקודש, the book does not get the status of a holy book that makes the hands טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The wisdom of שלמה, meaning his own human wisdom

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
Koheles does not make the hands impure,
because it is the wisdom of Shlomo.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from אסתר to a related question about קהלת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קהלת does not make the hands טמא because it is שלמה's own wisdom, not רוח הקודש.

steps.title: The חכמים prove קהלת came from רוח הקודש
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that שלמה said much more than what appears in קהלת. They also quote 'אל תוסף על דבריו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is this the only thing שלמה said? It already says, 'And he spoke three thousand proverbs.' And it also says, 'Do not add to His words.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי שמעון בן מנסיא. They argue that קהלת was said with רוח הקודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה said three thousand proverbs, but only a few were written down in תנ״ך. So the ones that were chosen must be special, meaning they came through רוח הקודש. The second פסוק, 'אל תוסף על דבריו', is brought as an extra proof, and the next step asks why it was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Was this all that he said?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וְכִי זוֹ בִּלְבַד אָמַר?
phrases.english: They said to him: Was this the only thing he said?
Wasn't it already stated:
"And he spoke three thousand proverbs",
phrases.notes: This פסוק is about שלמה, in מלכים א׳.

phrases.english: And it says: "Do not add to His words."
phrases.notes: A פסוק from משלי. 'And it says' means a second proof is coming.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וְכִי זוֹ בִּלְבַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון בן מנסיא's reason in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that קהלת is only שלמה's human wisdom
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Out of three thousand sayings, only some were written down, so the written ones must have come from רוח הקודש.

steps.title: Why was the second פסוק needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the second proof, introduced with 'ואומר', adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and it says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the חכמים needed a second פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually 'ואומר' means the first proof was not enough by itself. The גמרא wants to know what weakness in the first proof the second פסוק fixes.

phrases.english: What is the point of "and it says"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about how the proof in Step 14 is built.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the first פסוק alone was not enough

steps.title: The first proof could be pushed off, so 'אל תוסף' was added
steps.stepSummary: Someone could say שלמה chose on his own which sayings to write down. The פסוק 'אל תוסף על דבריו' shows that the written ones have a special status.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: he said a lot, and whatever he wanted was written down, and whatever he did not want was not written down. Come and hear: 'Do not add to His words.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the first proof alone could be pushed off. The second פסוק closes that gap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the first פסוק, one could argue that שלמה simply picked which of his own sayings to write, so being written proves nothing special. The warning 'אל תוסף על דבריו' shows that the written words carry a holy status that may not be added to, so they came from רוח הקודש.
steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים prove קהלת came from רוח הקודש with two פסוקים. The second, 'אל תוסף על דבריו', blocks the idea that שלמה just chose on his own what to write.

phrases.english: And if you would say:
As for speaking, he said a lot,
so that if he wanted, it was written,
and if he wanted, it was not written.
Come and hear: "Do not add to His words."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first פסוק could be explained as שלמה's own choice. 'אל תוסף על דבריו' shows the written words have a holy status.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: proof from what המן thought in his heart
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר proves that אסתר was said with רוח הקודש from the פסוק 'ויאמר המן בלבו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says that אסתר was said with רוח הקודש, as it says, 'And המן said in his heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with proofs that מגילת אסתר was said with רוח הקודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק reports what המן thought inside himself, which no person could have known. So the writer must have known it through רוח הקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: In his heart, meaning in his thoughts

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects to Step 9, where the גמרא said שמואל agrees that אסתר was said with רוח הקודש.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Esther was said with Divine inspiration,
as it says: "And Haman said in his heart."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to אסתר and brings proofs that it was said with רוח הקודש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אסתר was said with רוח הקודש, since it reveals המן's private thoughts.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: proof from everyone seeing אסתר with favor
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא proves that אסתר was said with רוח הקודש from the פסוק saying everyone who saw her liked her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says that אסתר was said with רוח הקודש, as it says, 'And אסתר found favor in the eyes of all who saw her.'
steps.whatsHappening: In the same ברייתא, רבי עקיבא gives a different proof for the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No person could know how every single person who saw אסתר felt about her. A statement about everyone's feelings could only be known through רוח הקודש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
Esther was said with Divine inspiration,
as it says:
"And Esther found favor
in the eyes of all who saw her."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: אֶסְתֵּר בְּרוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ נֶאֶמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second proof in the same ברייתא for the same idea as Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אסתר was said with רוח הקודש, since it reports how everyone who saw her felt.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's proof: מרדכי found out about the plot
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר proves that אסתר was written with רוח הקודש from the פסוק 'ויודע הדבר למרדכי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: ספר אסתר was said with רוח הקודש, as it says: 'And the matter became known to מרדכי.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third proof, after רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא, that מגילת אסתר was written with רוח הקודש. This one comes from רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is about the plot of בגתן ותרש to kill the king. רבי מאיר holds that how this secret reached מרדכי could only be known and written through רוח הקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Divine inspiration; the holy spirit that let the author know and write things beyond normal human knowledge
Was said, meaning the book was written or composed

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
The book of Esther was said with the Divine Spirit,
as it says: "And the matter became known to Mordechai."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֶסְתֵּר בְּרוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ נֶאֶמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another תנא's proof to the list started by רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אסתר was written with רוח הקודש, as shown by the פסוק saying the plot became known to מרדכי.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בן דורמסקית's proof: no one touched the plunder
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן דורמסקית proves that אסתר was written with רוח הקודש from the פסוק saying the Jews did not take the spoils.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בן דורמסקית says: ספר אסתר was said with רוח הקודש, as it says: 'But they did not lay their hands on the plunder.'
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth תנא, רבי יוסי בן דורמסקית, gives his own proof that מגילת אסתר was written with רוח הקודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jews fought their enemies in many places, and the פסוק says flatly that none of them took any spoils. Saying this with full certainty about so many people could only come through רוח הקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Plunder, the spoils taken from enemies
They stretched out their hand, meaning they took something

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben Durmaskit says:
The book of Esther was said with the Divine Spirit,
as it says: "But they did not lay their hands on the plunder."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹרְמַסְקִית אוֹמֵר: אֶסְתֵּר בְּרוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ נֶאֶמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as רבי מאיר, with a different פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אסתר was written with רוח הקודש, as shown by the פסוק saying no one took the plunder.

steps.title: שמואל's better proof: heaven confirmed what they accepted
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says he would have given a stronger proof: 'קיימו וקבלו' means heaven agreed above to what the Jews took on below.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: If I had been there, I would have said something better than all of them, as it says 'They confirmed and accepted.' This means they confirmed above, in heaven, what the Jews accepted below, on earth.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל, an אמורא who lived later, says that if he had been with the תנאים, he would have brought the strongest proof of all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two words: 'קיימו' (confirmed) and 'קבלו' (accepted). שמואל reads them as two places: the Jews accepted פורים on earth, and heaven agreed to it. No person could know what heaven agreed to without רוח הקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Above, in heaven / below, on earth

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the one proof רבא will say cannot be knocked down, so it becomes the main basis for saying מגילת אסתר has רוח הקודש.

phrases.english: Shmuel said: If I had been there,
phrases.notes: He means among the תנאים who gave the proofs above.

phrases.english: I would have said something better than all of them,
as it says: "They confirmed and accepted":
They confirmed above what they accepted below.
phrases.notes: Above means in heaven, and below means the Jews on earth taking on פורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אִי הֲוַאי הָתָם, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא מִלְּתָא דַּעֲדִיפָא מִכּוּלְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a proof he says is better than all four earlier proofs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אסתר was written with רוח הקודש, since only רוח הקודש could reveal that heaven confirmed what the Jews accepted.

steps.title: רבא: every proof can be refuted except שמואל's
steps.stepSummary: רבא says each proof has a weakness except שמואל's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: All of them can be refuted, except for שמואל's, which cannot be refuted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא judges all the proofs together. This is a setup line: next the גמרא will go through the proofs one by one to show how each one can be knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proof only works if the information could not have come from normal human knowledge. רבא claims every proof except שמואל's could be explained without רוח הקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation, a way to knock down a proof

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: לְכוּלְּהוּ אִית לְהוּ פִּירְכָא,
phrases.english: Rava said: All of them have a refutation,
except for Shmuel's, which has no refutation:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לְכוּלְּהוּ אִית לְהוּ פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from listing proofs to judging them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only שמואל's proof holds up; all the others can be refuted.

steps.title: Refuting רבי אליעזר: המן's thoughts were obvious
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows that anyone could have figured out what המן was thinking, so no רוח הקודש was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר's proof can be refuted. It is simple logic: there was no one as important to the king as המן. And when he went on and on describing the honor, he clearly said it with himself in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts going through the proofs, beginning with רבי אליעזר's proof from 'ויאמר המן בלבו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said only רוח הקודש could reveal המן's private thoughts. רבא answers that it was easy to guess: המן was the king's top official, and his long, detailed list of honors showed he wanted them for himself.

phrases.english: That of Rabbi Eliezer:
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 17: 'ויאמר המן בלבו', Haman thought in his heart that the king wanted to honor him.

phrases.english: it is logical reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא הֲוָה אִינִישׁ דַּחֲשִׁיב לְמַלְכָּא כְּווֹתֵיהּ,
phrases.english: that there was no person as important to the king as he was,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי כִּי קָא מַפֵּישׁ טוּבָא וְאָמַר —
phrases.english: and when this one went on at great length and spoke,
he was saying it with himself in mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out רבא's claim from step 22 on the first proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי אליעזר's proof from 'ויאמר המן בלבו'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: המן's thoughts could be figured out by plain logic and from his own words, so no רוח הקודש was needed.

steps.title: Refuting רבי עקיבא: each nation saw אסתר as its own
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי עקיבא's proof may be explained by רבי אלעזר: everyone saw אסתר as one of their own people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא's proof can be refuted. Perhaps it is like רבי אלעזר, who said: This teaches that each and every person saw her as a member of his own nation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now knocks down רבי עקיבא's proof from the פסוק that אסתר found favor in the eyes of everyone who saw her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said only רוח הקודש could know what everyone felt inside. רבא suggests that, according to רבי אלעזר, each person thought she came from his own nation. That kind of feeling people could show openly, so a human writer could know it.

phrases.english: That of Rabbi Akiva:
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 18, the פסוק that אסתר found favor with everyone who saw her.

phrases.english: perhaps it is like Rabbi Elazar, who said:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר, a different person from רבי אליעזר in the step before.

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נִדְמְתָה לוֹ כְּאוּמָּתוֹ.
phrases.english: It teaches that to each and every one she appeared as one of his own nation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's one-by-one refutations, moving from רבי אליעזר to רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי עקיבא's proof from 'ותהי אסתר נושאת חן בעיני כל רואיה'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק may describe something people could openly show, that each saw her as one of his own nation, so no רוח הקודש was needed.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רבי אליעזר (step 23) with רבי אלעזר (this step). They are different people, and here רבי אלעזר's teaching is used against רבי עקיבא's proof.

steps.title: מרדכי could have understood the plotters' language
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי מאיר's proof fails. מרדכי could have overheard בגתן ותרש because he knew their language.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the proof of רבי מאיר, that only רוח הקודש could reveal how מרדכי learned of the plot, can be answered with רבי חייא בר אבא's teaching: בגתן and תרש were Tarsians. They spoke in their own language, and מרדכי simply understood it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his list of weak proofs. Now he shows that רבי מאיר's proof from מרדכי discovering the plot did not need רוח הקודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר argued that the מגילה could only know about a secret plot through רוח הקודש. רבא answers that בגתן and תרש talked openly in their own language, thinking no one would understand. מרדכי knew that language, so a normal person could report the story.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; maybe (used to suggest another explanation)
The two servants who plotted to kill אחשורוש
Tarsians, people from a land with its own language

phrases.english: And that proof of Rabbi Meir —
perhaps it is like Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba,
who said: Bigtan and Teresh
were two Tarsians.
phrases.notes: So they spoke their own language, and מרדכי understood it. Nothing hidden was revealed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's step-by-step rejection of each proof, now aimed at רבי מאיר.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only רבי מאיר's proof, not the conclusion that אסתר was written with רוח הקודש.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plot could be known in a natural way: מרדכי understood the plotters' foreign language.

steps.title: Messengers could have reported that no spoils were taken
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי יוסי בן דורמסקית's proof fails. Messengers could have reported that the Jews did not take spoils.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the proof of רבי יוסי בן דורמסקית, that only רוח הקודש could know the Jews everywhere did not take spoils, can be answered: perhaps they sent messengers, who reported back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down the proof from step 20. He shows there was an ordinary way to know that no one took the spoils.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof said no human could know what happened in every city of the empire. רבא answers that messengers were sent around and brought the news back. So the information could come through normal reports.

phrases.english: And that proof of Rabbi Yosei ben Durmaskit —
perhaps they sent messengers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹרְמַסְקִית דִּלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in רבא's list of weak proofs.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only רבי יוסי בן דורמסקית's proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The fact that no spoils were taken could be learned from messengers.

steps.title: שמואל's proof has no answer
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes that שמואל's proof from 'קיימו וקבלו' cannot be knocked down.
steps.simpleTranslation: But שמואל's proof certainly has no refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting every other proof, רבא states his conclusion. שמואל's proof stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No human could know that heaven agreed above to what the Jews accepted below. There is no natural way to explain that knowledge. So only שמואל's proof truly shows רוח הקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; a weakness in a proof

steps.whatToRemember: Every proof that אסתר was written with רוח הקודש can be explained away except שמואל's: 'קיימו וקבלו', meaning heaven confirmed above what the Jews accepted below.

phrases.english: Shmuel's proof certainly has no refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up רבא's review, which began in step 22, by keeping שמואל's proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל's proof from 'קיימו וקבלו' is the one airtight proof that אסתר was written with רוח הקודש.

steps.title: One sharp pepper beats a basket of pumpkins
steps.stepSummary: רבינא uses a folk saying: one strong proof is better than many weak ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: This is what people say: one sharp pepper is better than a basketful of pumpkins.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא adds a popular saying to describe the result. שמואל's single proof is worth more than all the others put together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pumpkin is big but bland, and a pepper is small but powerful. Many proofs that can be explained away are like a basket of pumpkins. One proof that cannot be answered is like the sharp pepper.

keyTerms.meaning: That people say (introduces a folk saying)

phrases.english: Ravina said:
This is what people say:
Better is one sharp pepper
than a basketful of pumpkins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a folk saying to illustrate the conclusion of step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One strong proof is worth more than many weak ones.

steps.title: רב יוסף: פורים will never stop
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings another proof of רוח הקודש: the מגילה promises that פורים will never stop among the Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: the proof is from here: 'And these days of Purim shall not cease from among the Jews.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof that אסתר was written with רוח הקודש. This one comes from רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק promises that פורים will last forever. Only someone speaking with רוח הקודש could make a promise about the far future. So the book must be inspired.

keyTerms.meaning: Will not pass away; will not cease

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: from here:
"And these days of Purim"
"shall not cease from among the Jews."
phrases.notes: This is from אסתר chapter 9. Knowing that something will last forever is a prediction only רוח הקודש could make.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new proof for the same claim that שמואל and the others were proving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The promise that פורים will never stop shows the מגילה was written with רוח הקודש.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the memory will never end
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings his proof from the end of the same פסוק: the memory of פורים will not end from their descendants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק says: the proof is from here: 'Nor shall the memory of them perish from their descendants.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives his own proof. He uses the second half of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב יוסף, he points to a promise about the future. His words speak about the memory of פורים lasting through future generations. Only רוח הקודש could promise that.

keyTerms.meaning: Will not come to an end

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אוֹמֵר מֵהָכָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak says: from here:
"Nor shall the memory of them perish from their descendants."
phrases.notes: These are the closing words of the same פסוק רב יוסף quoted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אוֹמֵר מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel proof from the end of the same פסוק used in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The promise that פורים's memory will never end shows the מגילה was written with רוח הקודש.

steps.title: How many portions and how many gifts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's words 'ומתנות לאביונים' and brings רב יוסף's ברייתא: משלוח מנות is two portions to one person, and מתנות לאביונים is two gifts to two poor people.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה mentioned gifts to the poor. רב יוסף taught: 'And sending portions, a man to his friend' means two portions to one person. 'And gifts to the poor' means two gifts to two people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of רוח הקודש and goes back to a phrase from the משנה. It brings a ברייתא that sets the minimum amounts for the פורים מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'מנות' is plural, so at least two portions are needed, but 'רעהו' is one friend, so one person is enough. 'מתנות' is plural and 'אביונים' is plural, so two gifts must go to two different poor people, one each.

keyTerms.meaning: Gifts to the poor on פורים

steps.whatToRemember: משלוח מנות: at least two portions to one person. מתנות לאביונים: at least one gift each to two poor people.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two counts. For מתנות לאביונים, the two gifts go to two different poor people, not both to the same one.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the practical minimum of the two מצוות of the day of פורים that we keep today.

phrases.english: "And gifts to the poor."
Rav Yosef taught:
"And sending portions, a man to his friend" —
two portions to one person.
"And gifts to the poor" —
two gifts to two people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רוח הקודש discussion and returns to explain a phrase from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משלוח מנות requires two portions to one person. מתנות לאביונים requires two gifts to two poor people.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה sends a Purim gift to רבי אושעיא
steps.stepSummary: A story: רבי יהודה נשיאה sent רבי אושעיא a leg of a third-born calf and a jug of wine, and רבי אושעיא sent back a message.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה נשיאה sent רבי אושעיא the leg of a third-born calf and a jug of wine. רבי אושעיא sent him back a message:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing two portions being sent to one person, just like the ברייתא's definition of משלוח מנות. The last words set up רבי אושעיא's reply, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gift has exactly two kinds of food, meat and wine, sent to one person. That matches the rule we just learned: משלוח מנות means two portions to one person. The story stops at 'he sent him' so we can hear his answer next.

keyTerms.meaning: A thigh or leg of meat
A 'third' calf (רש״י: the third born to its mother)
He sent back to him (a message)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two 'sendings'. שַׁדַּר is the gift going from רבי יהודה נשיאה. שְׁלַח לֵיהּ is רבי אושעיא sending a message back.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה שַׁדַּר לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda Nesia sent to Rabbi Oshaya
phrases.notes: נְשִׂיאָה means he was the נשיא, the leader of the Jews in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: the leg of a third calf
phrases.notes: רש״י: 'עגלא תלתא – שלישי לבטן', the third calf born to its mother.

phrases.english: and a jug of wine.
He sent him back a message:

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה שַׁדַּר לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life story of the rule from Step 31: two portions sent to one person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An example of משלוח מנות: two kinds of food, meat and wine, sent to one person, followed by the recipient's reply.
